# ellmos-ai / ellmos-voice-io

> Local-first speech input, speech output, and wake-word helpers for LLM systems.

Last-checked: 2026-08-20
Test-suite: 24/24 passed (pytest, Python 3.12.10)
Version: 0.1.2

## Summary

`ellmos-voice-io` is a lightweight, LLM-neutral runtime module providing pluggable local-first primitives for Speech-to-Text (STT), Text-to-Speech (TTS), and Wake-Word detection. It operates strictly within caller-owned boundaries with zero background services, zero telemetry, and zero unrequested network calls.

## Key Architecture & Privacy Principles

- **Local-First & Offline Ready**: Core capabilities work completely offline without external cloud API dependencies.
- **Lazy & Optional Engines**: Engine libraries (Whisper, Vosk, pyttsx3, Piper, openWakeWord) remain lazy during construction and are only loaded when invoked.
- **Explicit Caller Ownership**: Callers explicitly control microphone permissions, audio retention, model storage paths, and audio playback.
- **Fail-Safe Privacy Boundary**: No hidden telemetry, no background listening daemons, and no database or telemetry dependencies.
- **Deterministic Lifecycles**: `WakeWordListener` checks stop events before accessing audio hardware and guarantees deterministic cleanup on exceptions.
- **Read-Only CLI Inspection**: `ellmos-voice-io status` outputs engine availability JSON without initializing hardware or downloading models.

## Engine Capabilities Matrix

| Primitive | Engine | Mode / Dependency | Characteristics |
|---|---|---|---|
| **STT** | `vosk` | Offline / Local Model | Offline speech-to-text with local model folder (`model_path` or `VOSK_MODEL`) |
| **STT** | `whisper` | Local / OpenAI Whisper | Neural STT with automatic or pre-loaded Whisper model sizes |
| **TTS** | `pyttsx3` | System Voices | Real-time audio playback or WAV/MP3/OGG file generation via OS voices |
| **TTS** | `piper` | Local ONNX Neural | Fast neural speech synthesis directly to audio files via explicit ONNX model |
| **Wake-Word** | `openwakeword` | Local Microphone | Caller-bound wake-word detection loop with explicit stop events and debouncing |
